annotation_provenance: Authored in a single session as NEW development material for Milestone 11-C's technical-competency extraction investigation. None of these sentences are drawn from evaluation/m11/corpus.json (M11) or evaluation/m11b/structured_qualification_controls.json (M11-B Stage 1) -- those remain cited only as DEVELOPMENT background, per M11-B's own established discipline. Every field below was decided from first principles (what the SENTENCE itself means, independent of any candidate extractor's output) BEFORE any extraction strategy in Phase 3 was implemented or run against this corpus -- there is no 'baseline outcome' column here the way M10E/M11-A1/M11-A2 had, because no live-parser detector exists for most of these categories to measure a baseline against (see docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_11_C_COMPETENCY_EXTRACTION.md Phase 1/1.4's own confirmation). This corpus is explicitly DEVELOPMENT material, never re-described as held-out -- see that document's own Phase 2 holdout-protocol section for the separate, unauthored holdout methodology.

schema_notes.text_category: named_technology | technical_competency | education | experience | nontechnical | responsibility | learning_opportunity | company_narrative | administrative | ambiguous -- the 9-way Phase 1 taxonomy PLUS named_technology, which Phase 1 treats as the already-solved baseline case
schema_notes.is_applicant_qualification: true | false -- decision A (does the text express an applicant qualification at all)
schema_notes.qualification_kind: a gitscore.jobs.parsing.qualification.QualificationKind value, or null when is_applicant_qualification is false
schema_notes.necessity: REQUIRED | PREFERRED | null (genuinely unknown/unresolved -- never a third value)
schema_notes.competency_concept: {'type':'competency_tag','id':'<slug>'} for a technical competency with no registry concept; {'type':'concept','id':'<registry id>'} for a named technology; null when neither applies
schema_notes.applicability_condition: null, or the exact conditional clause verbatim
schema_notes.github_observability: NOT_OBSERVABLE | PARTIALLY_OBSERVABLE | STRONGLY_OBSERVABLE | null (null only when is_applicant_qualification is false)
schema_notes.expected_conservative_projection: job_requirement | unparsed_claim -- the SAFE destination per project_qualification()'s own existing rules, not a recall target
schema_notes.sibling_qualifications: optional -- additional qualification objects the SAME sentence also implies, mirroring M11-B's own precedent for 'one sentence, multiple qualifications'

controls.text: Experience with Kubernetes is required.
controls.notes: Control baseline -- already fully solved by the existing parser, included to confirm the new extractor does not regress the already-working case.

controls.text: Strong understanding of algorithms and data structures is required.
controls.notes: Classic competency phrasing. A repository with algorithmic implementations (sorting, graph traversal) is a plausible but inconclusive proxy -- never proof.

controls.text: You should be comfortable reasoning about concurrency, race conditions, and lock-free programming.
controls.notes: Unusual wording ('you should be comfortable') -- no explicit 'required'/'must' marker, yet unambiguously REQUIRED in context (no hedge/preference language either).

controls.text: Deep knowledge of distributed systems, consensus algorithms, and fault tolerance is required.
controls.notes: Three related sub-competencies (distributed systems, consensus, fault tolerance) named in one sentence -- annotated as ONE competency claim (the sentence's own 'and' is listing attributes of a single area, not three independent requirements), contrast m11c-multi-02 below where splitting IS correct.

controls.text: Proven ability to design scalable system architecture for high-traffic services.
controls.notes: 'Proven ability' could also read as an EXPERIENCE claim (a track record) -- annotated TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY since the sentence names a specific technical domain (system architecture), not a bare years-of-experience claim.

controls.text: Experience debugging and optimizing performance-critical code paths.
controls.notes: Ambiguous necessity -- no REQUIRED/PREFERRED marker anywhere in the sentence or its (unspecified here) section context; genuinely unresolved, not guessable, so necessity=null is the honest annotation and the SAFE projection is UnparsedClaim, not a guessed REQUIRED row.

controls.text: Solid grasp of operating systems internals and TCP/IP networking fundamentals is required.
controls.notes: TCP/IP is arguably a 'named technology' in isolation, but here it modifies a broader competency claim ('networking fundamentals') -- annotated as the competency, not a specific_technology row, since the sentence is not asserting direct TCP/IP tooling usage.

controls.text: Experience designing normalized relational schemas and indexing strategies for large datasets.
controls.notes: Database DESIGN competency, distinct from naming a specific database technology (contrast m11c-tech-01-style PostgreSQL mentions). No necessity marker present -- ambiguous, annotated null.

controls.text: Understanding of ML fundamentals such as overfitting, regularization, and bias-variance tradeoff is a plus.
controls.notes: A conceptual-understanding competency with NO plausible GitHub evidence at all (unlike concurrency/system-design, which at least have weak implementation proxies) -- annotated NOT_OBSERVABLE, the sharpest TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY/observability contrast case after m11c-circuit-01.

controls.text: Experience with GPU programming and parallel computing paradigms is required.
controls.notes: Contrast with m11c-cuda-adversarial-01 below -- a specific CUDA dependency is never, by itself, proof of this broader competency.

controls.text: Background in digital signal processing, including FFTs and filter design, is required.
controls.notes: Engineering discipline outside typical software job postings -- generalization test case.

controls.text: Strong foundation in circuit theory and analog electronics is required.
controls.notes: The sharpest NOT_OBSERVABLE contrast -- a hardware-design domain with no software artifact possible regardless of specificity (M11-B's own m11b-competency-02 precedent, re-confirmed here in a new sentence).

controls.text: Experience designing firmware for resource-constrained embedded systems is required.
controls.notes: A firmware repository (RTOS usage, interrupt handlers, memory-constrained patterns) is a genuine, if imperfect, implementation proxy.

controls.text: Familiarity with control systems theory, including PID and state-space methods, is required.
controls.notes: 'Familiarity with' is normally a LOW-importance marker (importance.py) -- that axis is independent of necessity, which is still REQUIRED here ('is required' is explicit).

controls.text: Experience with computer vision techniques such as object detection and image segmentation is required.
controls.notes: 'Such as X and Y' illustrative framing (M11-B's own illustrative-vs-exhaustive distinction) -- OR_ANY, not AND, since object detection and image segmentation are offered as EXAMPLES of the broader competency, not two independently required sub-skills.

controls.text: Understanding of threat modeling, common attack vectors, and secure coding practices is required.
controls.notes: Security-review activity (CVE fixes, dependency-vulnerability commits) is a genuine, bounded proxy.

controls.text: Knowledge of digital logic design and Boolean algebra is required.
controls.notes: An HDL repository (Verilog/VHDL) is a genuine, bounded proxy -- unlike circuit theory's own NOT_OBSERVABLE (analog domain), digital logic has a direct software-adjacent artifact (the existing hdl.verilog concept).

controls.text: Candidates must demonstrate strong algorithmic problem-solving skills.
controls.notes: Genuinely unsectioned -- 'must demonstrate' is a local REQUIRED marker, so necessity/qualification_kind are both determinable from the local sentence alone (M10E's own existing precedent: a local marker always wins regardless of section origin).

controls.text: Experience with Python and a strong understanding of algorithmic complexity (Big-O analysis) are both required.
controls.notes: ONE sentence, TWO qualification objects (M11-B's own established precedent) -- the Python half is a SPECIFIC_TECHNOLOGY sibling, annotated separately below.

sibling_qualifications.note: the Python half of the same sentence -- already fully solved by the EXISTING parser, included here to confirm the competency extractor does not disturb it

controls.text: Required: strong skills in concurrency, distributed systems, and database design.
controls.notes: THREE independently-named, unrelated competency AREAS (contrast m11c-distsys-01's single area with three descriptive sub-terms) -- genuinely three sibling qualification objects, annotated here as the first with two more below.

controls.text: Experience with at least one of the following: distributed systems, concurrent programming, or high-performance computing.
controls.notes: 'At least one of the following' is the exhaustive-list idiom (M10D Root Cause 4's own ANY-of trigger phrase, re-applied here to competency tags rather than concept ids).

controls.text: Experience with algorithms and data structures, and familiarity with either distributed systems or high-performance computing.
controls.notes: An AND of (one fixed competency) and (an OR-group of two others) -- M10D's own Root Cause 6 shape, re-confirmed here for competencies. MIXED_UNSUPPORTED is the honest diagnostic value; routes to UnparsedClaim, the original text fully preserved, never falsely simplified.

controls.text: Our engineering team has deep expertise in distributed systems and has built some of the most resilient infrastructure in the industry.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: 'distributed systems' appears, but describes the EXISTING TEAM's own expertise, never the applicant -- a company-narrative sentence (M10E's own narrative-cue precedent), must not be extracted as a candidate qualification despite containing a real competency term.

controls.text: Design and implement distributed systems that scale to millions of users.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: a RESPONSIBILITY/duty bullet describing WHAT THE JOB ENTAILS DOING, never a stated applicant QUALIFICATION (Manulife's own M10E precedent, re-applied to a competency term instead of a soft-skill phrase). Must not be scored as a REQUIRED competency merely because it names one.

controls.text: You'll gain hands-on experience with distributed systems design and large-scale data processing.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: a LEARNING-opportunity promise (M10C's own LEARNING section kind, SOTI's own M10E precedent) -- never a requirement, regardless of the competency term it names.

controls.text: No prior experience with distributed systems is necessary -- we will train you.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: an EXPLICIT negation ('no prior experience... is necessary') -- the competency term is present but the sentence asserts the OPPOSITE of a requirement. The safest, most conservative behavior is to NOT extract a REQUIRED/PREFERRED competency row at all -- routing to UnparsedClaim never fabricates a false positive, even though it also does not yet recognize negation as its own first-class signal (see Phase 1.4/Phase 3's own limitation note: negation detection is a Phase 3 evaluation axis, not a guaranteed Phase 4 capability).

controls.text: Experience with GPU programming is required, unless you have equivalent experience with other forms of parallel computing.
controls.applicability_condition: unless you have equivalent experience with other forms of parallel computing
controls.notes: A material applicability condition -- Qualification CAN represent this (applicability_condition field), but project_qualification()'s own existing safety rule (Stage 1, unchanged) routes it to UnparsedClaim since JobRequirement has no field to hold the condition. The condition text survives verbatim in the UnparsedClaim's own text.

controls.text:
Strong understanding of
concurrency and
lock-free data structures is required.
controls.notes: Soft-wrapped across three physical lines, each ending in an ordinary content word with no comma/semicolon -- the SAME disclosed M11-A2 residual ambiguity, re-exercised here for a competency sentence; this corpus entry's TEXT is pre-joined (segmentation's own line-wrap behavior is tested elsewhere, M11-A2) so this control isolates the competency-recognition question from the segmentation question.

controls.text: Experience with quantum circuit design and qubit error correction is required.
controls.notes: A domain OUTSIDE the mission's own example list (quantum computing) -- the key generalization test: can the chosen strategy recognize this as TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY without having 'quantum' hardcoded, or does it fail silently to UNINTERPRETABLE/UNPARSED. Simulators exist but genuine quantum-hardware competency has no realistic GitHub proxy -- NOT_OBSERVABLE.

controls.text: We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive health benefits, and a 401(k) match.
controls.notes: Pure administrative/compensation text -- no competency term present at all, included as a baseline exclusion case.

controls.text: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field is required.
controls.notes: Already-solved baseline category, included to confirm the competency extractor does not relabel an education claim as a technical competency merely because it names technical FIELDS of study.

controls.text: 5+ years of professional software engineering experience is required.
controls.notes: Already-solved baseline category, included for the same reason as m11c-education-01.

controls.text: Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills are required.
controls.notes: Already-solved baseline category, included for the same reason.

controls.text: Experience with CUDA is required.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL/BOUNDARY CASE for Phase 5: this is a NAMED TECHNOLOGY claim (CUDA), not a competency claim -- the correct extraction is SPECIFIC_TECHNOLOGY, exactly as the existing parser already does. The adversarial point (tested in Phase 5, not by this row's own extraction) is that a candidate's CUDA repository dependency must NEVER be treated by any FUTURE evidence detector as proof of the SEPARATE 'GPU and parallel computing' competency (m11c-gpu-01) -- a technology mention is not evidence of the broader competency it merely uses.

controls.text: Experience with Python is required.
controls.notes: Same boundary point as m11c-cuda-adversarial-01: Python usage must never be treated as proof of the SEPARATE 'algorithms and data structures' competency (m11c-algo-01) by any future evidence detector.

controls.text: Experience with React is required.
controls.notes: Same boundary point: React usage must never be treated as proof of the SEPARATE 'system design and architecture' competency (m11c-sysdesign-01).

controls.text: Applicants should have hands-on experience with digital signal processing.
controls.notes: 'Should have' is a softer REQUIRED framing than 'must'/'required' -- annotated REQUIRED since there is no PREFERRED/hedge marker and the sentence is unconditional; a second, genuinely unsectioned example.

controls.text: Prior exposure to machine learning fundamentals and basic statistics is a plus.
controls.notes: Explicit PREFERRED marker ('a plus') -- also LOW importance by the existing importance.py table, an independent axis not re-annotated per-row in this corpus (Stage 1's own Qualification model carries no importance field at all, see M11-B's own documented scope).

controls.text: A strong technical background is required.
controls.notes: M11-B's own m11b-uninterpretable-01, re-confirmed here: genuinely unclear whether this means SPECIFIC_TECHNOLOGY, TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY, or EXPERIENCE -- UNINTERPRETABLE is the honest answer, not a forced guess at a specific competency tag.

controls.text: Must be technically proficient.
controls.notes: Even shorter and vaguer than m11c-ambiguous-domain-01 -- a second genuinely uninterpretable case, since 'technically proficient' names no domain at all.

controls.text: We're a small team solving hard problems in computer vision and machine learning at scale.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: a second company-narrative case naming TWO competency terms (computer vision, machine learning) describing the TEAM's own work, not an applicant qualification -- a harder case than m11c-narrative-01 since it has no 'our team has expertise' phrase, only a 'we're solving problems in X' framing.

controls.text: Debug and optimize performance-critical systems under tight latency constraints.
controls.notes: ADVERSARIAL NEGATIVE: second responsibility-bullet case, imperative mood ('Debug and optimize...') -- a duty description, not a qualification, despite naming the same competency as m11c-perf-01.

controls.text: Proficiency in one of the following areas: distributed systems, database internals, or operating systems.
controls.notes: Second exhaustive-list idiom case ('one of the following areas') -- contrast m11c-cv-01's illustrative 'such as' framing (exhaustive=false there).

controls.text: - Solid understanding of operating systems and process scheduling
controls.notes: A bare bulleted item with no local necessity marker at all -- necessity depends entirely on the (unspecified here) section's own hint; annotated null/UnparsedClaim to isolate the per-sentence competency-recognition question from section-level necessity inheritance (already covered by M10B/M10E).

controls.text: Please submit your resume and cover letter through our careers portal by March 15th.
controls.notes: Second administrative baseline exclusion case, no competency term present.
